newsitem.title: USA: White House expects to get CBO data this week.
newsitem.headline: White House expects to get CBO data this week.

text.p: The Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the White House bureau that drafts the budget, expects to receive the Congressional Budget Office's (CBO) economic assumptions this week, an OMB spokesman said Monday.
"We have not gotten them yet. We expect them sometime this week," the OMB spokesman said.

Historically, the White House and Congress have squabbled over whose economic assumptions are more reliable. To remove this as an area of dispute, the White House has pledged to produce a budget plan that balances according to either set.

OMB, which is in the midst of preparing President Bill Clinton's fiscal year 1998 budget proposal, has asked the CBO to provide the White House with both its economic assumptions and "technical" assumptions.
The economic assumptions, which forecast such items as expected rates of growth and inflation, are expected to be handed over this week.

The technical assumptions, which cover items like expected government tax revenues and spending on programs like Medicare and Medicaid, are not expected to be available until later, White House officials have said.
